title: What is SM-DP+ and how does it relate to my Openline eSIM?
body:
**SM-DP+** stands for *Subscription Manager – Data Preparation Plus*. It's the server that holds your eSIM profile between the moment we generate it and the moment your phone downloads it.

## What happens in practice

1. You buy an Openline plan. Our provisioning system asks our RSP partner to prepare a profile.
2. The prepared profile is uploaded to the SM-DP+ server and tagged with a matching activation code.
3. Your QR code encodes the **SM-DP+ address** (a hostname) plus the **activation code** (a per-order token).
4. Your phone connects to the SM-DP+ address, presents the activation code, and downloads the profile over TLS.

## Why does this matter to you?

Almost never — the whole flow is invisible. The one place SM-DP+ becomes user-visible is manual installation. If your QR code won't scan, your Openline email contains the SM-DP+ address and the activation code separately. Paste them into your phone's manual eSIM entry sheet and you're in.

title: What's the difference between SM-DP+ and SM-DS?
body:
Both are GSMA-standard servers in the eSIM ecosystem. They do different jobs.

- **SM-DP+ (Data Preparation Plus)** hosts and delivers a specific profile to a specific device via an activation code. This is what a travel eSIM like Openline uses today.
- **SM-DS (Discovery Server)** is a lookup service where a phone can ask "is there a profile waiting for me?" without a QR code. It's how some enterprise MDM systems push profiles silently.

## For Openline

We use SM-DP+ for all consumer plans; you always get either a QR code or a one-tap install link. SM-DS-based zero-touch provisioning is available in Openline for Business through our reseller API.

title: What is an eUICC and how much can it hold?
body:
The **eUICC** is the physical chip embedded in your phone that stores eSIM profiles — the modern equivalent of a plastic SIM card. It's a small piece of secure silicon, GSMA-certified, that talks to the modem.

## Capacity in practice

- **iPhones (XR and newer):** cache up to 8 eSIM profiles simultaneously; 2 can be active at once. iPhone 14 and newer in the US have no physical SIM slot at all.
- **Pixel 3 and newer:** 5–8 profiles cached, 2 active.
- **Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer:** 5+ profiles cached, 2 active.
- **Windows laptops with WWAN:** typically 4–8 profiles.

You can add and remove profiles freely; the chip re-uses freed memory. Openline never occupies more than one slot per plan.

title: What is an activation code (AC_Token) and why is it single-use?
body:
An **activation code** — sometimes called AC_Token in GSMA specifications — is a short string embedded in your QR code that unlocks *your* profile on the SM-DP+ server. Format: `1$smdp.example.com$XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`.

## Single-use, on purpose

The GSMA specification requires the SM-DP+ to invalidate an activation code the moment a device successfully downloads a profile with it. This prevents the same profile from being installed on multiple devices — an eSIM is device-bound by design.

If you accidentally scan the QR on the wrong phone, sign in at [openline.com](https://openline.com) and hit **Reinstall eSIM** to get a fresh code. The old one is dead the moment it's consumed.

title: What is LPA and why does it matter for eSIM install?
body:
**LPA** stands for *Local Profile Assistant*. It's the software on your phone that manages eSIM profiles — downloading, enabling, disabling, and deleting them. Every eSIM-capable device ships with an LPA; iOS calls it "Cellular Setup", Android surfaces it under SIMs.

## Why LPA matters for you

- When you scan an Openline QR, your phone's LPA reaches out to our SM-DP+ server and pulls the profile over TLS.
- If the LPA has a bug (occasionally happens with beta OS builds), install can fail even when your Wi-Fi and QR are both fine.
- Updating your OS keeps the LPA on the latest version — one reason we recommend running the latest patch before travelling.

title: Is Openline's traffic encrypted end-to-end?
body:
The path between your phone and Openline's infrastructure is encrypted like any modern cellular data connection:

- Between your phone and the partner radio: standard **AKA/EAP-AKA'** authentication and cellular ciphers (256-bit on 5G, 128-bit on LTE).
- Between the partner core and Openline's routing infrastructure: TLS inside GRX/IPX backhaul.
- Application-layer traffic (HTTPS websites, WhatsApp, Signal, etc.) is encrypted end-to-end by the app itself, on top of everything above.

## What that means

Openline sees byte counts, not content. We can't inspect the traffic; the partner network can only see aggregate volumes; the app-layer encryption is between you and the destination service. There is no man-in-the-middle at Openline.

title: What is IMSI and can I see it on my Openline eSIM?
body:
The **IMSI** (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) is a 15-digit number that identifies your subscription within a mobile network — like a username at the SIM level. Openline eSIMs each get one.

## Where to find it

- **iPhone:** it's not directly exposed; only network operators can query it.
- **Android:** dial `*#*#4636#*#*` and browse the Phone Information section on many phones (varies by OEM).
- **Openline app:** we don't display it because it changes when we roam you across partners. The stable identifier we use for support is the ICCID.

Unless you're doing IMSI-based routing yourself, you'll never need this value.

title: What is an MCC/MNC and why does Openline switch between them?
body:
**MCC** (Mobile Country Code) and **MNC** (Mobile Network Code) together identify a specific carrier in a specific country. For example, `310 260` is T-Mobile US; `234 15` is Vodafone UK.

## How Openline uses them

When your phone attaches to a partner network abroad, it reports the local MCC/MNC. Openline's multi-Tier-1 routing may hand you between partners over the course of your trip — you'll see the network name in the status bar change, but the Openline data plan is continuous.

If you're a network engineer curious about which partner you're on: **Settings → About phone → SIM status** on Android or **Settings → General → About → Carrier** on iPhone. That's the current MCC/MNC.

title: How does Openline's multi-Tier-1 network switching work?
body:
Openline's differentiator is **multi-Tier-1 switching**: in each country we connect you to whichever of 3–5 premium partners has the strongest signal *for your specific device at your specific location*.

## Under the hood

- Every Openline profile is provisioned with a **partner preference list** for each country. The order is dynamically maintained — we track signal quality across our customer base.
- Your phone's modem scans available networks. If a preferred partner is not visible or has weak signal, it falls to the next.
- Handovers between partners are handled at the RSP level, not the device level — your phone doesn't notice; you just see steady bars.

Most single-partner travel eSIMs pin you to one carrier per country. If that carrier's coverage is weak in your hotel or your neighbourhood, you're stuck. Openline's design avoids that failure mode.

title: What is a Tier-1 carrier and why does it matter?
body:
"Tier-1" is industry shorthand for a national mobile operator that owns and operates its own radio network — as opposed to an MVNO that resells another carrier's network. Vodafone UK, T-Mobile US, NTT DoCoMo, Telefónica are all Tier-1 in their countries.

## Why it matters for Openline

Tier-1s have the widest and deepest coverage in their country, including rural areas MVNOs don't reach. They're also the first to deploy 5G and the last to be de-prioritized during congestion.

Openline partners exclusively with Tier-1s for consumer plans — often multiple per country. That's the connectivity difference between "roaming" and "just works."

title: Does Openline support 5G Standalone (SA) or Non-Standalone (NSA)?
body:
Both, where the partner network supports them.

- **5G Non-Standalone (NSA)** overlays 5G radio on an LTE core. It's the most common 5G deployment worldwide as of 2026.
- **5G Standalone (SA)** uses a full 5G core, enabling network slicing, ultra-low latency, and better power efficiency on the device.

## What you'll see

- On NSA: status bar shows **5G** while the LTE control plane is still active. Speeds are 5G-fast.
- On SA: status bar may show **5G+**, **5G UC**, or similar. Speeds and latency are notably better.

Openline routing works transparently across both. Your device chooses the best mode available.

title: What is VoLTE and does Openline support it?
body:
**VoLTE** (Voice over LTE) is voice calls carried over the 4G/LTE data path instead of a dedicated 2G/3G voice channel. Since many countries have shut down 2G/3G (or are in the process), VoLTE has become essential for voice calls on modern phones.

## Openline's stance

Openline plans are **data-only** by design. We do not carry voice minutes to a number. Use WhatsApp, iMessage, FaceTime, Signal, Zoom, Google Meet, or any other data-app for voice — they all run natively over LTE/5G data.

Your **home carrier's** voice line continues to use its own VoLTE where the home carrier has a roaming agreement with a local network. That's separate from Openline.

title: What is Wi-Fi calling and does it work with Openline?
body:
**Wi-Fi calling** lets your phone route calls and SMS through Wi-Fi instead of a cellular tower. It's a feature of your home carrier's line, not of Openline.

## How to use it while abroad

- Keep Wi-Fi calling enabled on your home carrier's line (**Settings → Cellular → your home line → Wi-Fi Calling**).
- Connect the phone to any Wi-Fi.
- Calls to your home number ring on the phone as if you were home; SMS delivery works.

Openline handles the mobile data at travel prices. Wi-Fi calling handles voice/SMS on your home number over Wi-Fi. It's the cleanest split for international travel.

title: What is APN and do I need to set it manually for Openline?
body:
**APN** (Access Point Name) is the DNS-like handle your device uses to route data through a specific mobile network. Older SIMs required manual APN entry; modern eSIMs including Openline auto-configure it during install.

## When you might need to touch it

- On some Android builds after a full-phone reset, the APN doesn't reapply. Fix: create a new APN, name it **Openline**, set the APN field to **`openline`**, type **`default,supl,dun`**.
- iPhones never require manual APN for Openline; the profile carries it.
- If nothing else works, factory-reset the eSIM profile from openline.com — a fresh reinstall re-applies the APN too.

title: What is an EID and where do I find it?
body:
The **EID** (eUICC Identifier) is a 32-digit unique identifier for your device's eSIM chip. Openline doesn't need it for consumer purchases, but some enterprise integrations do.

## Where to find it

- **iPhone:** Settings → General → About → **EID**.
- **Android (Pixel):** Settings → About phone → **EID**.
- **Android (Samsung):** Settings → About phone → Status information → **EID**.
- **Universal fallback:** dial `*#06#`; swipe past IMEI to reveal EID on many phones.

Treat it as identifying information — don't share it publicly.

title: Can I have two Openline plans on the same iPhone at once?
body:
Yes. iPhone caches up to 8 eSIM profiles simultaneously; two can be active data lines at any given time.

## When this is useful

- One plan for the country you're currently in, one prepaid for your next destination.
- A backup plan you keep dormant until your primary runs out.
- A separate work plan you enable only during business hours.

## How to switch

**Settings → Cellular** → tap the plan you want as active data → toggle **Turn On This Line** → set **Cellular Data** to that plan. The other Openline plan stays installed but idle until you re-enable it.

title: Can Openline show up as my default carrier name in the status bar?
body:
No, and this is by design. Your phone shows the **partner network's** name in the status bar (Vodafone, KDDI, Movistar, etc.) because that's who the radio is actually attached to. Openline's name is only the profile label inside Settings.

If you want a cleaner status bar, rename the profile: **Settings → Cellular → the Openline line → Cellular Plan Label**. You can call it "Travel" or anything else, but the operator name shown while connected is still the partner's — that's the GSMA spec.

title: What GSMA specifications does Openline follow?
body:
Openline is built on the current GSMA eSIM specifications:

- **SGP.22 v3** — consumer remote SIM provisioning (RSP).
- **SGP.02 v4** — M2M / IoT profile management.
- **SGP.31** — the emerging IoT eSIM specification we're tracking for Openline Connect.
- **SGP.32** — eSIM IoT with the new IoT Profile Assistant (IPA) role.

We participate in the GSMA eSIM working group as a small operator; the connectivity standard we deploy for Openline Connect is built on top of these specs and open-sourced through our GitHub.

title: Openline shows Wi-Fi symbol but no cellular icon — what's wrong?
body:
When Wi-Fi is on, iOS shows the Wi-Fi glyph in the status bar instead of the cellular bars, even when cellular is fully connected. That's just how iOS's status bar works. Turn Wi-Fi off temporarily and you'll see the cellular icon and bars appear on the Openline line.

If you see **no bars at all** with Wi-Fi off, the line hasn't registered yet — try airplane mode toggle, then check that Data Roaming is on for the Openline line. If a partner network name shows next to the bars, cellular is fine and the "issue" is purely visual.

title: Why does my iPhone say 'No SIM available' when Openline is clearly installed?
body:
This error usually shows up when iOS has failed to load any eSIM profile at boot. It's rare and almost always cleared by a restart.

## Sequence to try

1. Airplane mode on for 30 seconds, then off.
2. Restart the iPhone (hold power + volume down; slide to power off).
3. Go to **Settings → Cellular** and confirm the Openline line is toggled on.
4. If it's still saying no SIM available, remove the profile (**Settings → Cellular → Openline → Remove eSIM**), then reinstall it from openline.com.

If reinstalling doesn't help, the RSP may have deprovisioned your specific profile due to a rare backend hiccup. Contact support with the ICCID and we'll re-issue.

title: My Openline works on Wi-Fi calling but cellular data shows 'No Service'
body:
Wi-Fi calling and cellular data are separate connections. Wi-Fi calling uses Wi-Fi to reach your home carrier's core; cellular data on Openline requires actual radio attachment to a partner network abroad.

## What to check

- Are you actually in a country covered by Openline? Wi-Fi calling works anywhere with internet, but cellular data needs local partner signal.
- Is **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line? Toggle it off and back on.
- Is **Cellular Data** set to Openline? Verify in **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data**.
- Try manually selecting a partner network in **Settings → Cellular → Openline → Network Selection**.

title: Openline installed cleanly but my status bar shows the home carrier's name instead
body:
Your phone shows the name of the line currently used for **voice calls**, not necessarily the one used for data. Even when Openline handles all your data, if you kept your home carrier's line as **Default Voice Line**, its name is what shows in the status bar (or its roaming partner's name, if the home line is abroad).

To see the actual Openline data connection: pull down Control Center and look at the cellular chip, or check **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data** — the label there is the true data source. If the label reads **Openline**, you're on Openline data regardless of the status bar.

title: Data works fine but my banking app won't open on Openline
body:
Some banking apps refuse to work over networks they consider "unusual" — including foreign carriers or perceived VPNs. The problem is on the bank's side, not Openline's.

## Fixes to try

- Open the bank's app on Wi-Fi first, complete any 2FA challenge, then switch back to Openline data.
- Whitelist the app in any content-blocker or MDM profile you might have on the phone.
- Contact the bank's support and mention you're travelling; some banks silently flag foreign SIMs and require a manual verification.

If a specific bank consistently blocks Openline, tell us. We track this and occasionally get IP ranges re-classified with the local partner network.

title: Why did my Openline plan run out of data faster than expected?
body:
Two common culprits: background app refresh and automatic photo/video backup. On a travel plan both can burn gigabytes overnight without you touching the phone.

## Quick audit

- **iPhone: Settings → Cellular → scroll down** to see per-app data usage on the current line. Reset counters before travel to make this useful.
- **Android: Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Openline → App data usage**.
- Turn off cellular data for photo apps, cloud backups, and streaming services during the trip.
- Turn off background app refresh entirely if the plan is small.

If your usage still looks unreasonable relative to what you actually did, contact us with the ICCID and rough time window — we can pull partner-level records.

title: Openline stops working when I plug my phone into CarPlay
body:
CarPlay itself doesn't affect cellular data, but some car systems disable the phone's Wi-Fi to prefer the car's own connection — and if the car isn't online, the phone can silently drop off cellular too. Wired CarPlay in particular has a known iOS bug where the modem restarts during connection.

## Fixes

- Toggle airplane mode after connecting to CarPlay to force a modem reset.
- If you're using wireless CarPlay, disconnect from the car's Wi-Fi hotspot for phone data.
- Update iOS and the car's firmware; both matter here.

title: Openline eSIM keeps dropping to 2G in the middle of nowhere
body:
That's coverage — rural areas away from Tier-1 5G/LTE cells may only offer 2G or 3G legacy service. Openline routes you to whatever the partner network offers, so if the partner has no 4G/5G presence, you'll drop to 2G.

## What to do

- Move toward a town centre if possible.
- Manually pick a different partner network in Cellular Settings — one Tier-1 may have better rural coverage than another.
- Some countries (Turkey, Egypt, parts of Africa) have shut down 2G/3G entirely; if you're in one of those and Openline can't hold LTE, the local coverage genuinely doesn't reach you here.

title: Why can't I receive iMessage on my home number while using Openline?
body:
iMessage is bound to your Apple ID and the phone numbers you've registered under it. If your home carrier's line loses signal or Wi-Fi calling is off, iMessage won't reach you via that number — Openline can't help because it's a separate line.

## Fixes

- Enable Wi-Fi calling on your home line before travelling.
- In **Settings → Messages → Send & Receive**, verify your Apple ID email is listed too — iMessage can arrive there even if the phone number is unreachable.
- Confirm your home number is still on the "You can be reached at" list.

title: Openline arrived by email but the QR code image is missing
body:
Some email clients (especially corporate Outlook or Gmail with aggressive image blocking) strip inline images by default. The QR is still in the email as an attachment or a link.

## What to do

- Open the email in a different client (Apple Mail, Gmail web).
- Click "Show images" or "Download attachments" if your client offers it.
- Sign in at [openline.com](https://openline.com) → **My eSIMs** → the plan → **Show QR code**. This works from any browser and is the canonical source.

title: Why does my Android phone say 'Network not registered' on Openline abroad?
body:
The message means the phone's radio isn't attached to any partner network. Possible causes: airplane mode, roaming disabled on the Openline line, wrong preferred network, or you're in a coverage gap.

## Order of operations

1. Airplane mode off, mobile data on.
2. **Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Openline**: turn on Data roaming.
3. Same menu → **Preferred network type**: set to 4G/LTE or 5G/LTE (avoid "2G only" unless you're desperate).
4. Force network scan: **More networks → Search now**.
5. Restart if the radio didn't attach after two minutes.

title: Can I use my Openline plan on a shared family device?
body:
Technically yes — an eSIM works the same regardless of who holds the device. But an Openline plan is single-device: you can't install the same QR on multiple phones simultaneously.

## Practical options

- **One family, one plan, one hotspot.** Buy an Unlimited plan and tether from one phone. Everyone connects via Wi-Fi.
- **One plan per phone.** Buy separate country plans; small ones (1 GB / 7 days) are cheap for lighter users.
- **Business account.** For teams travelling together, our business dashboard lets an admin buy plans in bulk and assign them per person.

title: Why does Openline show 5G but speed tests are LTE-level?
body:
Two possibilities:

1. **5G but limited backhaul.** Some 5G cells share backhaul with LTE and only deliver a modest bump in speed. Common in less-developed 5G markets.
2. **The speed test server is far away.** Even on 5G, hitting a server 5000 km away caps your throughput at ~200 Mbps due to TCP window scaling and latency. Try a local server.

If you're consistently below 20 Mbps on 5G in a major city, share the country, city, and time — we track this and escalate to the partner.

title: Openline eSIM registers on the phone but Cellular Plan Label field is blank
body:
Rare cosmetic bug that happens on iOS when a profile installs during a Wi-Fi drop. The profile is fine; the label just didn't sync.

## Fix

- **Settings → Cellular → the unlabeled line → Cellular Plan Label**.
- Type "Openline" and tap Done.

That's it. All the underlying data (ICCID, partner routing, roaming) is unaffected.

title: Openline works on my old phone but not on my new one after transfer
body:
Quick Transfer sometimes leaves partial state on the source device or the destination. The clean fix is a fresh reinstall.

## Steps

1. On the new phone, remove the Openline line (**Settings → Cellular → Openline → Remove eSIM**).
2. Sign in at [openline.com](https://openline.com) on any browser.
3. Open the plan → tap **Reinstall eSIM**. We issue a fresh QR.
4. Scan on the new phone using the Settings path, not the Camera.
5. Enable Data Roaming and set as Cellular Data.

If Reinstall fails or the new phone can't accept the profile, contact support with both device models and iOS versions.

title: My Openline eSIM works only when I toggle airplane mode after landing
body:
This is a phone-side quirk, not an Openline problem, but it's common enough that it's worth documenting. On some devices the modem doesn't re-scan networks aggressively enough after a long flight or between countries.

## Workarounds

- Toggle airplane mode as your first action after landing. It's a habit worth building.
- Set the preferred network type to Auto / LTE + 5G in Cellular Settings.
- Update to the latest phone firmware — modem drivers get quiet updates.

If it happens every single time, tell us the phone and OS; we track patterns and occasionally push partner-side fixes.

title: Why can't I disable my home carrier's roaming to force Openline data?
body:
Some home carriers (notably T-Mobile US "free" international roaming) auto-enable roaming and hide the switch. To make sure Openline handles data instead:

- **Settings → Cellular → your home line → Data Roaming**: turn it off. If the switch is greyed out, contact your carrier to disable it server-side.
- **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data**: explicitly set this to Openline (not "Allow Switching").
- **Turn off Allow Cellular Data Switching.**

Now the phone uses Openline for data no matter what your home carrier says.

title: Openline data works but VPN apps show 'connection failed'
body:
Most VPN apps work fine over Openline. When they don't, the issue is usually one of:

- **UDP blocked** by the partner network (some countries actively block WireGuard/OpenVPN UDP). Switch to TCP mode or a different protocol (IKEv2, Shadowsocks).
- **VPN server picks a home-country IP** that a captive portal rejects. Try a different endpoint in a neighbouring country.
- **DNS leak** — set the VPN to use its own DNS resolver.

If you rely on VPN for work and it's essential, test the specific combination before you travel.

title: Openline data works only in the browser, not in apps
body:
This is almost always a device-level content filter, MDM restriction, or misconfigured DNS — not an Openline issue.

## Debug order

1. Turn off any VPN, Content Blocker, or Focus Mode.
2. Verify no MDM (work-managed profile) is filtering traffic.
3. Change DNS to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 in your device settings.
4. Reset network settings (last resort — it clears saved Wi-Fi passwords too).

If step 3 fixes it, your original DNS was being blocked; keep the manual DNS. If it's still broken after step 4, the specific app has a hard-coded IP block. Contact the app's developer.

title: Why does my Openline eSIM disappear from Settings after I switch phones?
body:
When you transfer an eSIM (via Quick Transfer, iCloud restore, or Google's Data Transfer), the source phone deprovisions the profile — it disappears from its Settings. That's expected.

If you didn't intentionally transfer:

- Check the destination phone. If the eSIM was transferred by mistake, transfer it back.
- If it truly vanished, sign in at openline.com and **Reinstall eSIM**. We invalidate the ghost profile and issue a fresh one.

title: Managing Openline eSIMs via Microsoft Intune
body:
For Windows laptops and Windows 11 tablets, Openline profiles can be provisioned via **Microsoft Intune eSIM Cellular Profile** policies.

## Overview

1. Openline exports a list of activation codes matched to your device EIDs.
2. Your Intune admin creates a **cellular profile** with those activation codes.
3. Intune pushes the profile silently; the device downloads the eSIM at first check-in.

Contact **business@openline.com** to enable the enterprise API; the flow requires a signed Business Associate Agreement and volume commitment. Once set up, provisioning a new laptop is a one-line CSV upload from your admin's side.

title: Managing Openline eSIMs via Apple Business Manager
body:
For iPhones and iPads managed via **Apple Business Manager** and an MDM like Jamf, Kandji, Meraki, or Mosyle, Openline supports zero-touch eSIM provisioning through **SM-DS discovery** rather than QR codes.

## How it works

- Openline registers the target device EIDs in our SM-DS pool.
- The MDM instructs the device to discover pending eSIM profiles via `com.apple.esim.download` payload.
- The device pulls the profile silently and enables it.

Requires: iOS 17+, Apple Business Manager enrollment, and a supported MDM. Contact business@openline.com to enable enterprise provisioning.

title: Assigning Openline plans to specific employees
body:
In the Openline for Business dashboard, an admin can assign any plan to any team member by email. The assignee receives a personal delivery — QR code, one-tap install link, and setup instructions — under their own account.

## Where to do it

Dashboard → **Plans → Available** → the plan → **Assign** → select member. You can also bulk-assign via CSV upload if you have a big batch to distribute (say, a whole team leaving for a conference).

Unused assigned plans can be revoked and reassigned. Once activated they stay with the assigned user for the duration.

title: Revoking an Openline plan from a former employee
body:
If someone leaves the team while holding an active Openline plan, an admin can revoke it from the dashboard.

## Steps

1. Dashboard → **Plans → Active** → find the plan.
2. Click **Revoke**.
3. Choose whether the remaining time is refunded to your account balance or wasted (per plan terms).

The former employee loses access immediately; their phone's Openline line stops receiving data at the next network re-registration (usually within a few minutes).

title: SSO integrations for Openline Business
body:
Openline for Business supports **SAML 2.0** and **OpenID Connect** for single sign-on on the Growth and Enterprise tiers.

## Supported IdPs

- Okta
- Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD)
- Google Workspace
- JumpCloud
- OneLogin
- Ping Identity
- Any generic SAML 2.0 or OIDC provider

Setup is a 15-minute exchange of metadata URLs. Contact your Openline account manager to enable SSO on your workspace.

title: SCIM user provisioning for Openline Business
body:
On the Enterprise tier, Openline exposes a **SCIM 2.0** endpoint that your IdP can push user changes to automatically — new hires get an Openline seat, departing employees are deactivated, group memberships translate to Openline roles.

## Configuration

- Endpoint: `https://scim.openline.com/v2`
- Auth: Bearer token issued from your Openline dashboard
- Supported resources: `Users`, `Groups`

Standard Okta, Entra, and Google Workspace SCIM apps are certified. Contact enterprise support for a partner-specific setup guide.

title: Audit logging in Openline for Business
body:
Every admin action — plan purchase, plan assignment, plan revocation, member invite, member removal, SSO login — writes an entry to your workspace's audit log. Retained for 12 months on Growth and 24 months on Enterprise.

## Access

Dashboard → **Settings → Audit log**. Filter by actor, action type, date range. Export as CSV for compliance reviews.

We also stream audit events to your SIEM via webhook (Enterprise tier only). Ask your account manager to enable the webhook and provide a shared secret.

title: Data residency and export for Openline Business
body:
Business account data is stored in EU regions by default. Enterprise customers can request **US-only** or **APAC-only** residency if their data-classification policy requires it.

## Data export

Dashboard → **Settings → Privacy → Export data**. You get a signed ZIP with account details, orders, invoices, and audit logs in machine-readable formats. Delivery is instant for small tenants, up to 24 hours for large ones.

Full compliance details in the Trust Center: [openline.com/trust](https://openline.com/trust).

title: Best Openline plan for a 7-day trip to Japan
body:
For most first-time visitors, we recommend a **country plan** for Japan at 5–10 GB over 7–15 days. Openline routes across NTT DoCoMo, SoftBank, and KDDI, which gives excellent 5G coverage in Tokyo, Osaka, and Kyoto.

## Plan sizing

- **Business trip / light use:** 3 GB / 7 days.
- **Standard tourism (maps, rideshare, some streaming):** 10 GB / 15 days.
- **Heavy use + hotspot to a laptop:** Unlimited / 7 days.

## Local tips

- 5G is dense in central Tokyo, weaker in older suburbs. Openline hands you across partners as needed.
- Japan Rail Pass apps often need mobile data — install offline maps as backup.
- Convenience-store Wi-Fi is common if you want to conserve data.

title: Best Openline plan for a 2-week Europe trip covering 5+ countries
body:
A **Europe regional plan** wins here. One plan covers the EU, EEA, UK, Switzerland, and Turkey with no reactivation between borders.

## Plan sizing

- Casual sightseeing across cities: 10 GB / 30 days.
- Working remotely from cafes and Airbnbs: 20 GB / 30 days.
- Two travellers sharing via hotspot: Unlimited / 30 days.

## What to expect

- Openline hands you between Tier-1 partners at borders automatically.
- 5G is widely available in Germany, France, Spain, and Italy; 4G/LTE everywhere else.
- Rail travel through the Chunnel, Alpine tunnels, and mountain passes will drop signal briefly — normal.

title: Best Openline plan for South-East Asia island-hopping
body:
The **Asia regional plan** covers Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam with one activation.

## Plan sizing

- 2 weeks, moderate use, one country focus: country plan 10 GB / 15 days.
- 3 weeks, 3+ countries: Asia regional plan 20 GB / 30 days.
- Long backpacking trip with hotspots: Asia regional Unlimited / 30 days.

## Notes

- Remote islands (Gili, Palawan, southern Thai islands) often have only one Tier-1 partner. Signal on Openline is at least as good as any local SIM.
- Buy from Wi-Fi at your Bangkok/Singapore/Jakarta arrival lounge before flying to a smaller island.

title: Best Openline plan for a Latin America multi-country trip
body:
The **Americas regional plan** covers North, Central, and South America under one price point.

## Sizing

- Peru + Bolivia backpacking: regional plan 10 GB / 30 days.
- Mexico + Central America 3 weeks: regional Unlimited / 30 days.
- Business circuit São Paulo–Buenos Aires–Santiago: 5 GB / 15 days per city or regional if crossing borders.

Openline routes across Tier-1 partners; in Brazil that's Vivo/Claro/TIM, in Mexico it's Telcel/AT&T/Movistar, in Argentina Movistar/Claro/Personal. Coverage is very good in capitals, reasonable in mid-sized cities, and patchy in true rural areas.

title: Using Openline on the Camino de Santiago
body:
A Spain country plan or Europe regional plan works well for the Camino. You'll be in rural Galicia and northern Spain with mixed 4G coverage.

## What to expect

- **Coastal sections and cities (Santiago, León):** strong 5G.
- **Meseta and small villages:** 4G/LTE, occasional weak spots.
- **Mountain passes (O Cebreiro):** intermittent signal, sometimes only 3G. Download offline maps.

Battery packs matter more than a beefy data plan on the Camino. 5 GB is more than enough for two weeks if you're not streaming.

title: Using Openline for a US road trip
body:
Openline routes across AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon Tier-1 networks. In practice you're always on the strongest available signal.

## Sizing

- 1-week national park circuit: 10 GB / 15 days.
- 2-week cross-country drive: 20 GB / 30 days.
- Working remotely from RV parks: Unlimited / 30 days.

## Route tips

- Rural stretches (Nevada, Wyoming, Montana) will drop to LTE only; some areas have coverage from just one Tier-1. Openline's multi-partner routing gives you the best odds.
- Along Interstates you're rarely off-grid for long.
- National park visitor centres frequently have Wi-Fi.

title: Using Openline for a business trip to a single city
body:
For a short business trip, a country plan sized for your actual usage is the sharpest choice.

## Typical sizing

- 2 days, meetings + email only: 1 GB / 7 days.
- 3–5 days, video calls + rideshare: 3–5 GB / 7 days.
- Week-long with hotspot for laptop: 10 GB / 15 days.

## Business tips

- Set up 2FA to email as fallback in case SMS-to-home-number is unreliable.
- Enable Wi-Fi calling on your home line so clients can reach you on your normal number.
- Save your Openline receipt PDF as soon as you buy — expense-friendly.

title: Using Openline for a 1-day layover
body:
Even a short layover deserves connectivity — airport Wi-Fi is often gated behind email walls or capped.

## Recommended plan

- 500 MB / 1 day (where available) or 1 GB / 7 days is fine.
- Install before your flight; activation happens automatically when you land in a covered country.

Airports with strong Openline coverage: Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Singapore, Dubai, Istanbul, Doha, Seoul, Tokyo Narita/Haneda, LAX, JFK, LHR, CDG, GRU.

title: Using Openline while transiting via Dubai or Doha
body:
Both UAE and Qatar are Openline-covered; a plan will activate on arrival at Dubai (Etisalat/e& or du) or Doha (Ooredoo).

## Sizing

- 4-hour connection with lounge Wi-Fi backup: 500 MB / 1 day.
- Overnight stay: 1 GB / 7 days.
- Multi-city stopover: MENA regional plan 5 GB / 15 days.

## Notes

- Airport Wi-Fi in DXB and DOH is decent; you may not burn much data.
- If you exit airside to visit the city, Openline works citywide with strong 5G.

title: Using Openline on a Trans-Siberian rail journey
body:
Long rail journeys through Russia are complex — Openline coverage in Russia is limited and country plans may not be available. Check the country page on [openline.com](https://openline.com) before booking.

For rail travel that stays inside Openline's supported countries (Europe rail passes, Japan Shinkansen, Amtrak Northeast Corridor, Chinese HSR outside the tunnels), Openline works well. Expect signal drops in long tunnels; the phone reconnects on exit.

title: Using Openline for a Mediterranean cruise
body:
Cruises are the trickiest case: while at sea, cellular is only available through the ship's own maritime network at extremely high roaming rates. Openline (like all travel eSIMs) does **not** connect at sea.

## Best practice

- Turn **Data Roaming off** on the Openline line before you sail.
- Use the ship's Wi-Fi package while at sea.
- The moment you dock at any Openline-covered port, turn Data Roaming back on — your Openline plan works immediately.

You'll only burn Openline data while on land at each port, which is exactly what you want.

title: Using Openline for a Rocky Mountain / Banff trip
body:
Openline routes on Bell, Rogers, and Telus in Canada. Coverage in populated valleys is excellent; deep backcountry (interior of Banff, Jasper trails) is limited by radio physics, not by Openline.

## Sizing

- Base out of Banff/Canmore: 10 GB / 15 days.
- Multi-park driving: 20 GB / 30 days.
- Hut-to-hut hiking with SOS need: bring a satellite communicator; Openline alone won't reach the Bugaboos.

## Notes

- Icefields Parkway is patchy — download offline maps.
- Lake Louise has coverage at the lakeshore but not deep in the surrounding valleys.

title: Using Openline for a wildlife safari in East Africa
body:
Openline covers Kenya (Safaricom, Airtel) and neighbouring countries. In safari areas, coverage varies wildly by park and specific location.

## Where signal works

- **Nairobi and Mombasa:** strong 4G/5G.
- **Masai Mara:** partial coverage from Safaricom towers, patchy inside the reserve.
- **Serengeti (Tanzania):** limited coverage.
- **Amboseli, Tsavo:** better than the deep Mara.

Sizing: 10 GB / 15 days is enough for messaging, sharing photos, some video calls when in range. For blogging with photo uploads, go bigger. Consider a satellite communicator for true off-grid safety.

title: Using Openline for a Hajj or Umrah pilgrimage
body:
Openline covers Saudi Arabia (STC, Mobily, Zain) with strong 5G in Mecca, Medina, Jeddah, and Riyadh.

## Recommendations

- Mecca/Medina during peak season: Unlimited plan. Cellular congestion is extreme, and Openline's Tier-1 routing beats most alternatives.
- Group travel with shared hotspot: one Unlimited plan on the trip organiser's phone.
- Enable Wi-Fi calling on your home line so families can reach you at hotels.

Sizing tip: pilgrimage generates a lot of photo/video sharing. Budget 1 GB per day if that's a priority.

title: Using Openline while volunteering abroad
body:
Volunteer trips typically mean long stays in one country with modest connectivity needs.

## Sizing

- 1 month: Unlimited / 30 days (predictable) or 20 GB / 30 days (cheaper).
- 2–3 months: monthly Unlimited subscription, cancel any time.
- 6+ months: consider a local SIM in addition to Openline for a local phone number.

Openline stays with your home phone number reachable, which is important for family and emergency contact throughout the trip.

title: Using Openline as a solo female traveller
body:
Openline is designed to disappear once installed, which matters when you don't want to hand your phone to a local telco desk for a SIM swap.

## Safety tips

- Install before leaving home so you land connected. Bag snatchings sometimes target visible SIM-swap moments outside airports.
- Keep 2FA on the home line via Wi-Fi calling as a backup channel.
- Save embassy and local emergency numbers offline (Contacts, not just Notes).
- Share your itinerary and Openline eSIM plan expiry with a trusted person so they know when you're due to check in.

Openline never asks for an ID; your account is tied to an email only.

title: Japan — VoLTE requirement
body: Japan's carriers have phased out most 3G. Modern iPhones and Android flagships handle VoLTE natively over Openline data. If your device is more than 5 years old, some voice apps may not work reliably; use WhatsApp or LINE data-based calls instead.

title: Japan — Convenience-store Wi-Fi vs Openline
body: 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, and Lawson Wi-Fi is legit but usually requires an email sign-up per session. Openline is faster, always-on, and better if you're moving between shops.

title: Japan — Rail Wi-Fi vs Openline
body: JR East and JR Central Shinkansen have Wi-Fi that's usable but flaky in tunnels. Openline hands you across DoCoMo/SoftBank/KDDI seamlessly across the same route.

title: China — Openline vs China Mobile prepaid SIM
body: China Mobile prepaid SIMs require passport registration and are locked to a Chinese phone number. Openline is registration-free, keeps your home number, and — because we route through Hong Kong / Singapore — you can reach Google, WhatsApp, and YouTube without a VPN.

title: China — WeChat Pay on Openline
body: WeChat Pay works over Openline data. You still need a WeChat account with a Chinese bank card or a foreign credit card verified through the app — that's a WeChat problem, not an Openline one.

title: China — Alipay Tour Pass on Openline
body: Alipay Tour Pass (which lets foreigners top up local yuan) works fine over Openline data. Install and verify it before leaving your home country or you may hit KYC delays.

title: USA — 5G Standalone rollout
body: US Tier-1 5G-SA deployment is fastest on T-Mobile, then Verizon, then AT&T. Openline routes you to the strongest, so 5G-SA availability varies by city. Los Angeles, New York, Miami, and Seattle have wide 5G-SA.

title: USA — Emergency 911 on Openline
body: Every US phone can call 911 regardless of eSIM state, as long as any cellular signal is present. Openline is data-only and not intended for voice, but 911 is guaranteed at the radio layer.

title: UK — Wi-Fi calling with UK carriers
body: EE, O2, Vodafone UK, and Three UK all support Wi-Fi calling for their subscribers. If your UK home line is with one of them, you can be reached on your UK number over any Wi-Fi while Openline handles data.

title: UK — Openline vs local UK MVNO SIM
body: For a UK trip specifically, a Giffgaff or Lebara SIM is cheap for month-long stays. Openline is better for shorter trips or if you want to keep your home number active.

title: France — eSIM in TGV tunnels
body: TGVs pass through several long tunnels (notably Alpine sections). Signal drops entirely inside; Openline reconnects on exit. Not an eSIM issue — same for local SIMs.

title: Why did my crypto payment for Openline underpay by a few cents?
body: Crypto network fees eat into what actually arrives at the destination wallet. If we detect underpayment, we credit your Openline account for the amount received and message you to top up the difference — no lost funds.

title: How long does BTC confirmation take for an Openline order?
body: Bitcoin mainnet takes 10–30 minutes for 1–3 confirmations on a typical fee. Openline waits for a single confirmation before fulfilling, so your eSIM arrives within 10–15 minutes of your payment appearing in the mempool.

title: How long does Ethereum confirmation take?
body: Ethereum takes seconds to a few minutes depending on gas price. Openline releases the eSIM after 1 confirmation on the destination chain — usually under 60 seconds after your send.

title: How does Openline handle stablecoin depegs?
body: For USDT payments, we lock the USD-equivalent price at the moment you check out. If USDT depegs slightly between checkout and confirmation, that's on the market — the eSIM ships based on your locked price.

title: Can I get a refund to a different crypto wallet than I paid from?
body: Yes. Contact ask@openline.com with the original transaction ID and the wallet address you want the refund sent to. We handle it manually and cover the outbound network fee.

title: Does Openline charge FX conversion fees?
body: No. Prices display in your local currency where possible; if your card issuer converts, they apply their FX rate. Openline itself takes no conversion cut.

title: Why did my Klarna Openline order fail?
body: Klarna has minimum-amount thresholds by country and rejects orders where the shipping-address country doesn't match the card issuer. Try a different payment method or contact Klarna support.

title: Why did my iDEAL Openline order stay stuck 'processing'?
body: iDEAL sometimes takes up to 15 minutes on weekends. If it's stuck past an hour, contact billing@openline.com with the order ID and we'll trace it with the acquiring bank.

title: How do I request a corporate purchase order for Openline?
body: Contact business@openline.com with your legal name, VAT ID, PO template, and expected volume. We accept POs on Growth and Enterprise business tiers with net-30 or net-60 terms depending on credit review.

title: Can I split a single Openline order across multiple invoices?
body: Not on consumer orders. On business accounts, admin can group orders and issue consolidated monthly invoices for cleaner expense reporting.

title: Why do I see two charges on my Apple Pay for one Openline order?
body: Apple Pay sometimes shows an authorization hold plus the settled charge on your issuer statement. The hold drops in 1–3 business days without affecting your balance. If both charges settle, contact billing — we refund duplicates instantly.

title: Can I get a receipt in a language other than English?
body: Yes. In **Account → Billing → Preferences** choose your invoice language: English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, or Korean.

title: Why did my American Express card get declined for Openline?
body: AmEx sometimes flags EU merchants for cardholders outside the EU. Call AmEx to whitelist Openline (Bulgaria) or use Apple Pay / PayPal instead — same underlying card, different transaction path.

title: Do Openline discounts stack with referral credits?
body: Not on the same order. Pick whichever is bigger; unused referral credit stays in your balance for a future order.

title: Where can I download historical invoices?
body: **Account → Orders** shows your full history. Each order has a Download Invoice (PDF) button. Business accounts get a bulk-export CSV in Dashboard → Reports.

title: Can Openline generate a proforma invoice before I pay?
body: Yes on business orders. Contact your account manager or business@openline.com with the plan mix, quantity, and billing details — we issue the proforma within a business day.

title: Why did I get charged VAT when I entered my company's VAT ID?
body: VAT ID validation happens at checkout via VIES. If VIES was temporarily down or your ID had a typo, the fallback is to charge VAT. Contact billing@openline.com with a screenshot; we refund the VAT and re-issue as reverse-charge.

title: How does Openline handle chargebacks?
body: Every chargeback is investigated by our billing team. We provide the acquiring bank with proof of service (activation logs, ICCID, partner records). If the chargeback succeeds despite that, the associated account is suspended pending review.

title: Install Openline on iPhone SE (3rd gen)
body:
Openline installs cleanly on **iPhone SE (3rd gen)**. It supports eSIM, dual-line, and modern iOS features like Data Roaming per line.

## Install steps

1. On the iPhone SE (3rd gen), connect to Wi-Fi.
2. Open the Openline confirmation email on a second screen (a laptop, tablet, or the iPhone SE (3rd gen) itself for one-tap install on iOS 17.4+).
3. Tap the install link, or in Settings → Cellular → Add Cellular Plan → scan the QR from your email.
4. Follow the iOS prompts; label the line **Openline**.
5. Turn **Data Roaming on** for the Openline line and set it as **Cellular Data**.

## Notes for iPhone SE (3rd gen)

- Openline supports 5G on iPhone SE (3rd gen) where the partner network deploys it.
- Dual-line is supported — your home eSIM (or physical SIM on older models) can stay installed alongside Openline.
- Wi-Fi calling on the home line continues to work when Openline is active.

title: Install Openline on Google Pixel 8a
body:
Openline works on the **Google Pixel 8a** through the standard Android eSIM install flow.

## Install steps

1. Connect the Google Pixel 8a to Wi-Fi.
2. Open Settings and find the eSIM section — the exact path varies by OEM. Common paths:
   - Samsung: **Settings → Connections → SIM manager → Add eSIM**
   - Google/OnePlus/Motorola: **Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Add eSIM**
   - Xiaomi: **Settings → SIM cards & mobile networks → Add eSIM**
3. Scan the QR code from your Openline email, or paste the manual activation code.
4. Confirm and label the plan **Openline**.
5. Enable **Data roaming** for the Openline line.
6. Set **Mobile data** to Openline.

## Notes for Google Pixel 8a

- Restart the Google Pixel 8a once after install if the network doesn't register within 60 seconds.
- APN is set automatically; if data doesn't come up, add an APN named `openline` manually.
- Dual-eSIM is supported — you can keep your home eSIM installed alongside.

title: Install Openline on Microsoft Surface Pro 11
body:
The **Microsoft Surface Pro 11** has a built-in WWAN modem with eSIM support. Openline installs directly through Windows 11's cellular settings.

## Install steps

1. Connect the Microsoft Surface Pro 11 to Wi-Fi.
2. Open **Settings → Network & Internet → Cellular → Manage eSIM profiles**.
3. Click **Add profile** → **Let me add a profile manually**.
4. Paste the SM-DP+ address and Activation Code from your Openline confirmation email.
5. Save and turn the profile on.

## Notes for Microsoft Surface Pro 11

- Enterprise customers can push Openline profiles silently via Microsoft Intune (see the MDM articles in this KB).
- The eSIM survives Windows updates but not full "Reset this PC" flows — reinstall from openline.com afterwards.
- If cellular doesn't come up after install, restart the modem: Settings → Network → Cellular → toggle Cellular off/on.

4. Paste the SM-DP+ address and Activation Code from your Openline confirmation email.
5. Save and turn the profile on.

## Notes for Dell Latitude 9450 (5G)

- Enterprise customers can push Openline profiles silently via Microsoft Intune (see the MDM articles in this KB).
- The eSIM survives Windows updates but not full "Reset this PC" flows — reinstall from openline.com afterwards.
- If cellular doesn't come up after install, restart the modem: Settings → Network → Cellular → toggle Cellular off/on.

title: Using Openline in Cambodia
body:
Openline works across **Cambodia** on the local Tier-1 partner networks we have signed. Coverage focuses on the capital and major urban centres; smaller towns are LTE/4G through a single partner.

## What to expect

- **Speed:** 4G/LTE in most urban areas; 5G where the country's carriers have rolled it out (typically in the capital and a handful of secondary cities).
- **Coverage:** dense in cities, thinner in rural areas — Openline routes to whichever Tier-1 has signal.
- **Latency:** low enough for messaging and video calls in urban zones; may spike in remote regions.

## Choosing a plan

- **Short stay (1–7 days):** country plan, 1–3 GB / 7 days.
- **Standard visit (1–2 weeks):** country plan, 5–10 GB / 15 days.
- **Extended stay / remote work:** Unlimited / 30 days, or the appropriate regional plan if you're combining with neighbours.

## Local tips

- Install before flying and toggle airplane mode on landing to force a fresh scan.
- Data Roaming must be **on** on the Openline line at all times — travel eSIMs technically roam, but Openline is never billed as roaming to you.

title: Can I install Openline on a Steam Deck?
body: Steam Deck is Wi-Fi only — no cellular modem. Openline can't install on it directly. The right pattern is to run Openline on your phone and use it as a Wi-Fi hotspot for the Steam Deck.

title: Can I install Openline on an Apple Watch?
body: No, cellular Apple Watches use a special provisioning bound to your paired iPhone's carrier. Openline is a separate travel line and does not extend to the Watch. Use your Watch over Bluetooth to your Openline-connected iPhone instead.

title: Can I use Openline as a permanent home data connection?
body: Technically yes on monthly Unlimited, but that's not what we optimize for. Openline is designed for travel. For always-on home internet, a fixed line or fixed-wireless plan from a local ISP is cheaper.

title: Can I stack multiple Openline promotions on one order?
body: No — one discount code per order. Referral credit stacks separately with any active promotion.

title: Can I gift an Openline plan to someone else?
body: Yes. At checkout, enter the recipient's email as the delivery address. They become the account holder for that plan; you get the receipt.

title: Can I resell Openline plans on my own website?
body: Only through our official Reseller API. Bulk-buying consumer plans and reselling them violates the terms; the plans will be deactivated on discovery. Contact partners@openline.com for legitimate reseller access.

title: Do you have an SLA for the Openline API?
body: Growth and Enterprise business tiers include SLA commitments: 99.9% API uptime, 99.5% eSIM activation success rate within 60 seconds. Consumer plans get best-effort with a public status page.

title: Can I whitelist Openline IPs for corporate firewalls?
body: Business customers can request the current partner network IP ranges. Note that these ranges change as we add or rotate partners; a firewall based on IPs is fragile. Consider DNS-based egress controls or Zero Trust proxying.

title: Is there an Openline Slack app?
body: Yes on business plans. Install from the Openline dashboard; the Slack app lets team members request plans in-channel, admins approve inline, and expiry alerts land in Slack.

title: How do I unsubscribe from Openline marketing emails?
body: Every marketing email has an unsubscribe link at the bottom, or go to **Account → Preferences → Email**. Transactional emails (receipts, expiry alerts) cannot be unsubscribed while you have an active account — they're operational.

title: Where can I download Openline's brand assets for a press article?
body: The public media kit is at [github.com/paulfxyz/openline-brand-assets](https://github.com/paulfxyz/openline-brand-assets). Includes logos, wordmarks, colours, and usage guidelines. Press contact: press@openline.com.

title: How is Openline different from Airalo?
body: Airalo is an eSIM marketplace: they resell profiles from many partners under Airalo branding. Openline is a next-gen operator: we own the routing, switch you across 3–5 premium partners per country automatically, and price aggressively against wholesale. The practical difference: Openline gives you the strongest of several networks, not just one.

title: How is Openline different from Holafly?
body: Holafly emphasises unlimited plans and country-focused branding. Openline shares the unlimited approach but adds multi-Tier-1 routing (so you're never stuck on one weak partner), no throttling of Unlimited plans, and crypto payment support out of the box.

title: How is Openline different from Saily?
body: Saily is NordVPN's travel eSIM. Openline shares the modern-app philosophy but is independent of any VPN company, focuses on Tier-1 partnerships rather than budget MVNOs, and offers a broader plan matrix including regional plans.

title: What happens to my Openline plan if you go out of business?
body: Openline operates under EU consumer protection rules. In the (extremely unlikely) event of insolvency, EU customers have a claim against pre-paid but undelivered service; consumers outside the EU can dispute the charge through their card issuer. We're building for the long haul; investor materials and financial position are shared with institutional investors on request.

title: What ports does Openline block?
body: None. Openline is a normal cellular data path; local partner networks may have their own filters (some block SMTP outbound, for instance), but Openline itself doesn't add filters on top.

title: Can I run a Tor exit node over Openline?
body: Technically the protocol works, but running a Tor exit node on a mobile eSIM is impractical: NAT prevents inbound connections, and any high-volume anonymity traffic will look like abuse to our partner networks. Tor client use for privacy is fine.

title: Can I run a VPN server on my Openline connection?
body: Same answer as Tor exit node: NAT and mobile IP rotation make it impractical. For inbound reachability, use a hosted VPS as your VPN endpoint and connect *to* it over Openline data.

title: Does Openline support IPv6-only carrier networks?
body: Yes. Some Openline partners deploy IPv6-only cores with NAT64 for legacy IPv4 traffic. Your device gets an IPv6 address; IPv4-only destinations are reached transparently. If you notice a specific IPv4-only service failing, tell us — we can escalate.

title: What is Openline's stance on customer data and law enforcement?
body: We disclose data to law enforcement only when compelled by valid legal process in the jurisdiction we operate in (Bulgaria/EU). We publish an annual transparency report with anonymised counts of requests, jurisdictions, and outcomes. We push back on overbroad or extraterritorial requests.

title: VoLTE requirement in Turkey
body:
Turkey's Tier-1s (Turkcell, Vodafone TR, Türk Telekom) have shut down 3G. Your device must support VoLTE on Turkish LTE bands (Band 1, 3, 7, 8, 20) for calls to work reliably. Most flagship devices from 2020+ do; some regional variants may not.

## Practical check

Before travelling, verify your device advertises VoLTE support for the destination's bands. Google "Does [your phone model] support VoLTE in Turkey?" or check the manufacturer's spec sheet.

If your device doesn't support the local VoLTE profile:

- Data (Openline) still works normally.
- Voice apps (WhatsApp, Signal, FaceTime, Zoom) work fine because they ride the data path.
- Traditional voice calls to a phone number may fail — but Openline doesn't provide those anyway, so this matters only for your home carrier's line while roaming.

title: Buying an Openline eSIM for Afghanistan
body:
To use Openline in **Afghanistan**, buy a plan in the Openline app or website before you fly — the eSIM installs immediately and activates the moment you land and enable Data Roaming. In Afghanistan, coverage is limited to the government-controlled cities and even there networks are unstable, so we recommend a small starter data plan.

## Steps

1. Open the Openline app and search for "Afghanistan".
2. Pick a data plan sized for the length of your stay — most travellers pick a 7- or 30-day option.
3. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or supported crypto.
4. Install the eSIM immediately via the one-tap sheet (iPhone) or QR code (Android).
5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

## Local details

The regulated currency is **AFN**, but you always pay in USD or EUR when buying Openline. Rates listed in the app already include local taxes and roaming fees, so there is nothing added at the border.

title: What networks does Openline use in Afghanistan?
body:
In Afghanistan, coverage is limited to the government-controlled cities and even there networks are unstable, so we recommend a small starter data plan. Coverage inside Kabul is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Afghanistan means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Afghanistan but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Afghanistan**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — coverage is limited to the government-controlled cities and even there networks are unstable, so we recommend a small starter data plan. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Afghanistan?
body:
Every Openline plan that lists Afghanistan in its coverage table works on arrival — you don't pick a "Afghanistan plan", you pick a **region** or **global** plan and Afghanistan is included. Most travellers going to Afghanistan pick either the Central Asia regional plan or the Global plan.

## Which to pick

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.
- **Regional plans** (e.g., Central Asia) are ideal if you cross borders — e.g., a road trip.
- **Global plans** cover 130+ countries and are the right choice if you split trips across continents.

All Openline plans are prepaid, don't auto-renew, and never charge you overage — when you're out of data you can top up in the app in seconds.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Afghanistan?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Afghanistan is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Afghanistan, coverage is limited to the government-controlled cities and even there networks are unstable, so we recommend a small starter data plan.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Afghanistan start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Algeria but no data

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Argentina?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Argentina is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Argentina, we roam on Movistar and Personal; both cover Buenos Aires, Bariloche, Mendoza and Ushuaia with 4G, 5G only in a few CABA neighborhoods.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Argentina start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: What networks does Openline use in Armenia?
body:
In Armenia, Team (Ucom) and Viva-MTS both accept Openline profiles; expect fast LTE in Yerevan and reliable coverage on the road to Sevan and Dilijan. Coverage inside Yerevan is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Armenia means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Armenia but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Armenia**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — team (ucom) and viva-mts both accept openline profiles; expect fast lte in yerevan and reliable coverage on the road to sevan and dilijan. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Bermuda but no data
body:

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — one communications is our partner; lte covers the entire island and most of the surrounding boat routes. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: What networks does Openline use in Canada?
body:

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Canada but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Canada**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — we roam on bell and rogers; 5g in every major city plus the trans-canada highway; lte almost everywhere else including yukon and coastal newfoundland. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

If you have bars but no data in **Ecuador**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — claro ec and movistar both carry us; lte in quito, guayaquil, cuenca and the galápagos; 3g on the amazon side. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Ecuador?
body:
Every Openline plan that lists Ecuador in its coverage table works on arrival — you don't pick a "Ecuador plan", you pick a **region** or **global** plan and Ecuador is included. Most travellers going to Ecuador pick either the South America regional plan or the Global plan.

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.
- **Regional plans** (e.g., South America) are ideal if you cross borders — e.g., a road trip.
- **Global plans** cover 130+ countries and are the right choice if you split trips across continents.

All Openline plans are prepaid, don't auto-renew, and never charge you overage — when you're out of data you can top up in the app in seconds.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Ecuador?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Ecuador is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Ecuador, Claro EC and Movistar both carry us; LTE in Quito, Guayaquil, Cuenca and the Galápagos; 3G on the Amazon side.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Ecuador start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: Buying an Openline eSIM for Egypt

5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

title: What networks does Openline use in Egypt?
body:

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Egypt means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

If your home carrier is EU-based and Guyana is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Guyana, GTT and Digicel Guyana carry us; LTE in Georgetown and the coastal strip; interior jungle mostly has no coverage.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Guyana start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: Buying an Openline eSIM for Haiti
body:
To use Openline in **Haiti**, buy a plan in the Openline app or website before you fly — the eSIM installs immediately and activates the moment you land and enable Data Roaming. In Haiti, Digicel Haiti carries us; LTE in Port-au-Prince, Cap-Haïtien and Jacmel, though political instability can cause outages.

## Steps

1. Open the Openline app and search for "Haiti".
2. Pick a data plan sized for the length of your stay — most travellers pick a 7- or 30-day option.
3. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or supported crypto.
4. Install the eSIM immediately via the one-tap sheet (iPhone) or QR code (Android).
5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

## Local details

The regulated currency is **HTG**, but you always pay in USD or EUR when buying Openline. Rates listed in the app already include local taxes and roaming fees, so there is nothing added at the border.

title: What networks does Openline use in Haiti?
body:
In Haiti, Digicel Haiti carries us; LTE in Port-au-Prince, Cap-Haïtien and Jacmel, though political instability can cause outages. Coverage inside Port-au-Prince is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Haiti means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Haiti but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Haiti**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — digicel haiti carries us; lte in port-au-prince, cap-haïtien and jacmel, though political instability can cause outages. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Haiti?

If you have bars but no data in **Kenya**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — safaricom is our primary partner; lte across nairobi, mombasa, kisumu, the maasai mara and the coast; 5g in nairobi and mombasa. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Kenya?
body:
Every Openline plan that lists Kenya in its coverage table works on arrival — you don't pick a "Kenya plan", you pick a **region** or **global** plan and Kenya is included. Most travellers going to Kenya pick either the East Africa regional plan or the Global plan.

## Which to pick

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.
- **Regional plans** (e.g., East Africa) are ideal if you cross borders — e.g., a road trip.
- **Global plans** cover 130+ countries and are the right choice if you split trips across continents.

All Openline plans are prepaid, don't auto-renew, and never charge you overage — when you're out of data you can top up in the app in seconds.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Kenya?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Kenya is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Kenya, Safaricom is our primary partner; LTE across Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, the Maasai Mara and the coast; 5G in Nairobi and Mombasa.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Kenya start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: Buying an Openline eSIM for Kiribati
body:
To use Openline in **Kiribati**, buy a plan in the Openline app or website before you fly — the eSIM installs immediately and activates the moment you land and enable Data Roaming. In Kiribati, ATHKL is our partner; LTE on Tarawa, 3G on outer atolls; some islands still have 2G only.

## Steps

1. Open the Openline app and search for "Kiribati".
2. Pick a data plan sized for the length of your stay — most travellers pick a 7- or 30-day option.
3. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or supported crypto.
4. Install the eSIM immediately via the one-tap sheet (iPhone) or QR code (Android).
5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

## Local details

The regulated currency is **AUD**, but you always pay in USD or EUR when buying Openline. Rates listed in the app already include local taxes and roaming fees, so there is nothing added at the border.

title: What networks does Openline use in Kiribati?
body:
In Kiribati, ATHKL is our partner; LTE on Tarawa, 3G on outer atolls; some islands still have 2G only. Coverage inside Tarawa is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Kiribati means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.
