To use Openline in **Lebanon**, buy a plan in the Openline app or website before you fly — the eSIM installs immediately and activates the moment you land and enable Data Roaming. In Lebanon, Alfa and Touch both carry us; LTE in Beirut, Tripoli, Byblos and the Bekaa; power outages can cause brief tower downtime.

## Steps

1. Open the Openline app and search for "Lebanon".
2. Pick a data plan sized for the length of your stay — most travellers pick a 7- or 30-day option.
3. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or supported crypto.
4. Install the eSIM immediately via the one-tap sheet (iPhone) or QR code (Android).
5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

## Local details

The regulated currency is **LBP**, but you always pay in USD or EUR when buying Openline. Rates listed in the app already include local taxes and roaming fees, so there is nothing added at the border.

title: What networks does Openline use in Lebanon?
body:
In Lebanon, Alfa and Touch both carry us; LTE in Beirut, Tripoli, Byblos and the Bekaa; power outages can cause brief tower downtime. Coverage inside Beirut is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Lebanon means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Lebanon but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Lebanon**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — alfa and touch both carry us; lte in beirut, tripoli, byblos and the bekaa; power outages can cause brief tower downtime. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Lebanon?
body:
Every Openline plan that lists Lebanon in its coverage table works on arrival — you don't pick a "Lebanon plan", you pick a **region** or **global** plan and Lebanon is included. Most travellers going to Lebanon pick either the Middle East regional plan or the Global plan.

## Which to pick

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.
- **Regional plans** (e.g., Middle East) are ideal if you cross borders — e.g., a road trip.
- **Global plans** cover 130+ countries and are the right choice if you split trips across continents.

All Openline plans are prepaid, don't auto-renew, and never charge you overage — when you're out of data you can top up in the app in seconds.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Lebanon?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Lebanon is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Lebanon, Alfa and Touch both carry us; LTE in Beirut, Tripoli, Byblos and the Bekaa; power outages can cause brief tower downtime.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Lebanon start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Luxembourg?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Luxembourg is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Luxembourg, POST and Orange LU both carry us; 5G across the whole grand duchy and into the Belgian and German borders.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Luxembourg start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: Buying an Openline eSIM for Macau
body:
To use Openline in **Macau**, buy a plan in the Openline app or website before you fly — the eSIM installs immediately and activates the moment you land and enable Data Roaming. In Macau, CTM and China Telecom Macau carry us; LTE across the peninsula and Coloane, 5G on the strip.

## Steps

1. Open the Openline app and search for "Macau".
2. Pick a data plan sized for the length of your stay — most travellers pick a 7- or 30-day option.
3. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or supported crypto.
4. Install the eSIM immediately via the one-tap sheet (iPhone) or QR code (Android).
5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

## Local details

The regulated currency is **MOP**, but you always pay in USD or EUR when buying Openline. Rates listed in the app already include local taxes and roaming fees, so there is nothing added at the border.

title: What networks does Openline use in Macau?
body:
In Macau, CTM and China Telecom Macau carry us; LTE across the peninsula and Coloane, 5G on the strip. Coverage inside Macau is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Macau means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Macau but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Macau**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — ctm and china telecom macau carry us; lte across the peninsula and coloane, 5g on the strip. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Republic of the Congo?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Republic of the Congo is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Republic of the Congo, Airtel Congo and MTN Congo carry us; LTE in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Republic of the Congo start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: Buying an Openline eSIM for Réunion
body:
To use Openline in **Réunion**, buy a plan in the Openline app or website before you fly — the eSIM installs immediately and activates the moment you land and enable Data Roaming. In Réunion, Orange and SFR carry us at French mainland pricing; LTE across the island and up to the volcano.

## Steps

1. Open the Openline app and search for "Réunion".
2. Pick a data plan sized for the length of your stay — most travellers pick a 7- or 30-day option.
3. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or supported crypto.
4. Install the eSIM immediately via the one-tap sheet (iPhone) or QR code (Android).
5. On arrival, turn **Data Roaming** on for the Openline line.

## Local details

The regulated currency is **EUR**, but you always pay in USD or EUR when buying Openline. Rates listed in the app already include local taxes and roaming fees, so there is nothing added at the border.

title: What networks does Openline use in Réunion?
body:
In Réunion, Orange and SFR carry us at French mainland pricing; LTE across the island and up to the volcano. Coverage inside Saint-Denis is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Réunion means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Réunion but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Réunion**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — orange and sfr carry us at french mainland pricing; lte across the island and up to the volcano. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Sweden but no data
body:

In Tuvalu, TTC is our partner; LTE in Funafuti, 3G on outer atolls. Coverage inside Funafuti is the strongest and speeds are typically comparable to a local prepaid line.

## Network behavior

- Your phone auto-selects the best available partner — you don't pick a network manually.
- If you see "No Service" in a remote area, toggle airplane mode; sometimes the phone latches onto a weaker roaming partner and needs a reselect.
- VoLTE (HD voice) support depends on the partner. Data-only plans don't need VoLTE; if you're using a plan with voice, we tell you in the plan detail.

## What "coverage" means for you

Openline coverage in Tuvalu means data throughput, DNS resolution, and low-latency access to global services. Streaming, maps, messaging and banking apps all work as they would at home — we don't throttle specific app categories.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Tuvalu but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Tuvalu**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — ttc is our partner; lte in funafuti, 3g on outer atolls. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Tuvalu?
body:
Every Openline plan that lists Tuvalu in its coverage table works on arrival — you don't pick a "Tuvalu plan", you pick a **region** or **global** plan and Tuvalu is included. Most travellers going to Tuvalu pick either the Oceania regional plan or the Global plan.

## Which to pick

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.
- **Regional plans** (e.g., Oceania) are ideal if you cross borders — e.g., a road trip.
- **Global plans** cover 130+ countries and are the right choice if you split trips across continents.

All Openline plans are prepaid, don't auto-renew, and never charge you overage — when you're out of data you can top up in the app in seconds.

title: Should I use Openline or my home carrier's roaming in Tuvalu?
body:
If your home carrier is EU-based and Tuvalu is an EU/EEA member, you're already inside Roam-Like-At-Home and don't need Openline for data. Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Tuvalu, TTC is our partner; LTE in Funafuti, 3G on outer atolls.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Tuvalu start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

Openline runs alongside your home line — you keep your number for SMS/2FA and use Openline for data.

title: My Openline eSIM has signal in Zambia but no data
body:
If you have bars but no data in **Zambia**, the fix is almost always the Data Roaming toggle. On the Openline line — not your home line — turn **Data Roaming ON** in your phone's cellular settings. Then confirm Openline is selected as **Cellular Data**.

## Full checklist

1. **Data Roaming** ON for the Openline line.
2. **Cellular Data** set to Openline.
3. **Airplane mode** off, then briefly toggle it on and off to force a fresh registration.
4. **Restart** the phone if the toggle doesn't take effect after 60 seconds.
5. **APN**: leave it blank on iPhone; on Android it should auto-provision but you can set it to `openline` if the app tells you to.

If none of the above works, you're probably in a partner-coverage dead zone — mtn zambia, airtel zambia and zamtel carry us; lte in lusaka, livingstone, kitwe and ndola. Move a few hundred meters and try again.

title: Which Openline plans work in Zambia?
body:

- **Single-country plans** exist for high-volume destinations and give you the best per-GB price.

Everywhere else, Openline is almost always dramatically cheaper. In Zambia, MTN Zambia, Airtel Zambia and Zamtel carry us; LTE in Lusaka, Livingstone, Kitwe and Ndola.

## Rough comparison

- **US/UK/AU home carriers** charging daily-pass roaming typically cost $10–15/day — Openline plans in Zambia start at a fraction of that.
- **EU home carriers** outside the EU zone typically fall back to per-MB pricing that can hit €10+/MB — Openline avoids all of it.
- **Chinese, Indian, and Latin American home carriers** vary widely; even so, an Openline plan is usually cheaper and doesn't require you to opt in to a roaming pack at home.

title: How do I know if my phone supports Openline?
body:
Almost every phone released after 2019 supports eSIM, and the Openline app runs a full compatibility check the moment you sign up — you don't have to guess.

## Fast checks

- **iPhone**: any iPhone XS or newer sold outside mainland China supports eSIM. US iPhone 14 and newer are eSIM-only.
- **Android**: Pixel 3 and newer, Samsung Galaxy S20 and newer (most regions), most Xiaomi flagships from 2022, OnePlus 11 and newer.
- **Not supported**: physical-SIM-only devices, some MVNO-locked handsets, and older Huawei models sold in China.

If our compatibility checker misses a restriction on your device and your Openline plan doesn't install, that's on us — we refund it in full.

title: How long does it take to activate an Openline eSIM?
body:
From "tap to buy" to "connected to the internet" is usually under two minutes on iPhone and under four minutes on Android. The eSIM profile downloads in seconds; the slow part is your phone registering with a local network once you land.

## Timing details

- **Purchase**: <30 seconds (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or crypto)
- **Install**: 20–60 seconds — a one-tap sheet on iOS 17.5+ or a QR scan on Android
- **First network attach on arrival**: 15 seconds to 3 minutes — depends on the country and how busy the tower is
- **Data working**: the moment your phone shows 4G/5G on the Openline line

If activation takes longer than 5 minutes after landing, toggle airplane mode once to force a fresh registration.

title: Where is Openline based?
body:
Openline is a fully remote company with team members across Europe, North America and Asia. Legal entity is registered in the EU, which means we're subject to GDPR and the EU eIDAS framework for identity — good news for you as a customer.

## What that means practically

- Data-protection requests go through EU DPA channels
- Support is available in English, French, Portuguese, Spanish, German and Italian
- Company hours span multiple time zones, so response times don't have big gaps

title: Can I buy an Openline plan without installing the app?
body:
Yes — every plan on openline.com is fully purchasable in your browser. The app is a convenience for managing multiple plans and getting install shortcuts, but it's not required.

## Web flow

1. Open **openline.com** and pick a plan.
2. Pay with card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or crypto.
3. We email you a QR code and a one-tap install link that works on iOS 17.5+ and Android 13+.
4. Install, then follow the standard on-arrival Data Roaming toggle.

The web checkout also supports guest purchase — you don't need an account for the first plan, though creating one makes reinstalls and refunds a lot simpler.

body:
Our support team answers in English, French, Portuguese, Spanish, German and Italian. We can handle most other European and Asian languages via machine-assisted translation with a human review, so feel free to write in whatever you're comfortable with.

- **In-app chat**: fastest path, staffed 24/7 for critical activation issues

title: How quickly does Openline support respond?
body:
Median response time is under 15 minutes for in-app chat and under 4 hours for email. Activation-blocking issues (you're at the airport and the eSIM won't install) are prioritized and typically answered in under 5 minutes.

- Attach a screenshot of the Cellular settings pane
- Include the ICCID number of the affected eSIM (visible in Settings → Cellular → Openline)

title: How do I change my Openline account language?
body:
Open the Openline app, tap your profile icon, and pick **Language** — the change applies instantly. On the website, click your avatar in the top-right and pick from the language dropdown.

## Which languages are available

We currently ship the full UI in English, French, Portuguese, Spanish, German, Italian, Dutch and Japanese, with more coming. Support content (this KB) is being translated in the same order.

title: How do I enable dark mode in the Openline app?
body: Openline follows your system theme by default — turn on dark mode in iOS/Android and the app switches automatically. If you want to force one theme regardless of system, go to **Settings → Appearance** in the app and pick Light, Dark or System.

title: Is Openline a licensed telecom operator?
body:
Openline operates as a Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) through partnerships with licensed carriers in every country we serve. The eSIM profile you install is issued by a GSMA-accredited Remote SIM Provisioning (RSP) infrastructure, and the roaming agreements are held by our upstream partners.

## Practical implications

- You benefit from the same regulatory protections as any licensed operator's customer
- Emergency calls (112 in EU, 911 in US, 999 in UK) work on any available network regardless of your Openline plan status
- Data-protection is governed by GDPR since our legal entity is EU-based

title: Does Openline share my data with home-country authorities?
body:
We only respond to lawful requests from EU authorities (where our legal entity is registered) or from authorities in the country where the roaming traffic terminates, and only via the proper legal channels. We publish a transparency report annually.

## What data we hold

- Account: email and payment method (never the full card)
- Usage: aggregate GB per country per plan, retained for billing dispute windows
- Not held: your IP address history, browsing metadata, or per-app usage

title: How can I make my Openline plan last longer?
body:
The two highest-leverage changes are turning off background app refresh for large apps (Photos sync, Google Drive backup, iCloud Photos, Netflix pre-downloads) and picking a lower streaming quality where you don't need HD. Everything else — email, messaging, maps, banking, ride-sharing — barely moves the needle.

## Save the most, fast

- **Turn off cloud photo backup** while abroad. This alone can save several GB per week.
- **Set streaming apps to Data Saver** (Spotify, YouTube, Netflix, Instagram, TikTok)
- **Download offline maps** for Google Maps or Organic Maps before you fly
- **Skip auto-play** in social apps — the biggest silent GB drain

title: Does Openline count data used for iOS/Android system updates?
body:
Yes — any bytes that cross the cellular radio count against your Openline plan, including OS updates, iCloud sync and Google Play Store updates. That's true of every eSIM and every cellular carrier, not just Openline.

## How to avoid it

- **Turn off** Cellular Data for the App Store, iCloud, Photos and Drive apps while abroad. Wi-Fi still works, just not cellular.
- **Postpone iOS updates** by declining "Install Tonight" — the update will wait for Wi-Fi
- **Android**: in Google Play Store → Settings → Auto-update apps, pick "Over Wi-Fi only"
